everyday-time-words.title: maten, aswè, jòdi a, kounyeya
everyday-time-words.bodyMarkdown:
Useful everyday time expressions include:

- **maten** — morning
- **aswè** — evening
- **jòdi a** — today
- **kounyeya** — now

You already know **kounyeya** from current actions. Now connect these words with a wider everyday schedule.

tomorrow-and-routine.title: denmen maten and chak jou
tomorrow-and-routine.bodyMarkdown:
Two more useful everyday expressions are:

- **denmen maten** — tomorrow morning
- **chak jou** — every day

At this level, treat them as useful time chunks. You do not need advanced future or scheduling grammar.

schedule-conversation.title: Jan and Mari compare schedules
schedule-conversation.bodyMarkdown:
**Jan:** Mari, akilè ou etidye kreyòl?

**Mari:** Senkè. Mwen etidye kreyòl aswè. E ou menm?

**Jan:** Mwen etidye kreyòl lendi maten.

**Mari:** Èske ou travay chak jou?

**Jan:** Wi, mwen travay chak jou.

This combines familiar questions, routines, and time without adding advanced tense grammar.

schedule-now-review.title: schedule vs. kounyeya
schedule-now-review.bodyMarkdown:
Listen to one more exchange.

Jan gives a clock time for his routine, then answers what he is doing **kounyeya**.

Notice how familiar action and time phrases work together in the same exchange.
